input.content: Pattern: ownership-guard removal before a mutating pop in cleanup code. In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), a guard `association = store.active.get(workspace_id); if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id: store.active.pop(...)` was replaced by an unconditional `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)` under the guise of "simplification". The guard enforced that only the setup that OWNS the current active association may evict it. Removing it causes a stale/superseded cleanup (e.g. cleaning up an old or never-activated setup B) to evict the active association belonging to a DIFFERENT setup A for the same workspace. Symptom: a live workspace silently loses its active setup. Lesson: a dict.pop(k, None) being null-safe does not make removing an identity/ownership check safe — the check guarded WHICH value may be removed, not WHETHER the key exists. Review heuristic: when a cleanup/delete simplification drops a `== id` / ownership comparison, treat it as a behavior change (wrong-entity deletion), not a refactor.
